statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14661 (PostgreSQL dblink and subscriptions can append to arbitrary files): the sslkeylogfile connection option, passed through dblink or CREATE/ALTER SUBSCRIPTION, makes libpq append NSS keylog lines to a file the user chooses. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14661/ lists 16.16 as the fixed release for major version 16 and says releases before PostgreSQL 18 are affected if libpq 18 or later is installed and used by the server; the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_16_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/f7b12b9f7d62f9ab83af0b72383a8684bece33d3 (Security: CVE-2026-14661; master commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/08010fa4f43dc06b701592e605b548eaf07fd5f7), in tag REL_16_16 and not in REL_16_15. It adds a check that dblink, postgres_fdw and libpqwalreceiver run on the connection options before connecting, which refuses any option not on an allowed list with "permission denied to set connection option"; libpqwalreceiver skips the check for the server's own primary_conninfo and for physical replication connections. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, lists CVE-2026-14661 under 16.16-r0 in its secfixes. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on that branch and the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the current 16.16-r0 build uses the APKBUILD at that commit. None of its patches changes the C sources or headers the fix changes; its external-libpq patch edits only src/Makefile and src/Makefile.global.in so that the build links against the system libpq instead of building its own. The libpq-18 condition holds here: in every published build for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0) on x86_64 and aarch64, /usr/lib/postgresql16/libpqwalreceiver.so in postgresql16 and /usr/lib/postgresql16/dblink.so in postgresql16-contrib list libpq.so.5 as NEEDED, and the only package providing libpq.so.5 in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository is libpq built from PostgreSQL 18 (18.1-r0 to 18.7-r0). In those builds the "permission denied to set connection option" message is in libpqwalreceiver.so, dblink.so and postgres_fdw.so in 16.16-r0 only, while 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 lack it; /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres in each reports the matching PostgreSQL release. 16.16-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14661, the sslkeylogfile connection parameter letting a user of dblink or CREATE/ALTER SUBSCRIPTION append data to a file of their choosing, in 17.12. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14661/ lists 17.12 as the fixed release for major version 17 and says versions before 18 are affected when libpq 18 or later is installed and in use by the server; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14661. dblink.so, postgres_fdw.so and libpqwalreceiver.so (used by subscriptions) are in the postgresql-17 package of every published build on amd64 and arm64 and link libpq.so.5. The libpq5 package published from this source in the DHI Debian repository is built from PostgreSQL 17, and the 17.11-1 and 17.12-0 packages carry their own libpq.so.5.17 from the same release, so these builds do not ship libpq 18; because a server can be run against a libpq 18 installed from elsewhere, the builds before 17.12 are still recorded as affected, following upstream's table. The postgres server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix, and 17.12-0 is the lowest published build that does. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
